assessment.presenting_problem:
Patient is a 37-year-old female presenting with severe polysubstance use disorder involving IV fentanyl, alcohol, and
benzodiazepines. Admitted following opioid overdose requiring naloxone administration in the ED. Patient reports using IV
fentanyl 1-2g daily, drinking approximately 750mL-1L vodka daily, and taking 4-6mg alprazolam daily from multiple
sources. Patient states "I wasn't trying to kill myself, I just wanted everything to stop — the nightmares, the shaking, all of
it." Co-occurring PTSD and Major Depressive Disorder with chronic passive suicidal ideation.
2. Signs and Symptoms (DSM-V-TR based) resulting in impairment(s):
(Include current examples for treatment planning, e.g., social, occupational, affective, cognitive, physical)
Social: Patient is isolated, estranged from mother, limited contact with brother. Only significant relationship is with
boyfriend who is an active user and perpetrator of intimate partner violence. No recovery community, no sponsor, no
sober supports. Occupational: Unemployed 18 months, terminated from pharmacy technician position following diversion
investigation. Unable to maintain employment due to substance use. Affective: Persistent depressed mood, anhedonia,
tearfulness, severe anxiety, constricted affect. PHQ-9: 18 (moderately severe). GAD-7: 15 (severe). Cognitive: Intermittent
confusion regarding timeline of recent events, poor concentration, low insight and impaired judgment. Reports difficulty
with decision-making. Physical: Underweight (BMI 18.2), track marks bilateral antecubital fossae and left hand, elevated
liver enzymes (AST 187, ALT 142), thrombocytopenia (platelets 98K), Hepatitis C positive. CIWA-Ar 18, COWS 14 on
admission.

DOB: 04/09/1989
Provider: andrew c
Appointment: Individual appointment on May 12, 2026
6:00 pm - 6:50 pm CT, 50 min
Billing code: 90834 - Psychotherapy, 45 min
DAP Note
Data
Follow-up session for ongoing treatment of polysubstance use disorder (IV fentanyl, alcohol, benzodiazepines), co-
occurring PTSD, and Major Depressive Disorder. Patient is on Day 8 of medically managed intensive inpatient treatment.
Withdrawal management is progressing — CIWA scores have been below 10 for past 48 hours. Patient has begun engaging
in group programming.
Assessment and Response
Social: Patient remains isolated from healthy supports. Boyfriend continues to send coercive text messages oscillating
between affection and threats. Patient has not responded per staff recommendation but is distressed by the contact.
Brother in Denver remains supportive via phone. Occupational: Remains unemployed, unable to address vocational needs
while in acute treatment. Affective: Mood described as "up and down." Tearful when discussing relationship and trauma
content. Anxiety remains elevated, particularly in evenings — patient identifies this as her typical time of use. PHQ-9: 16
(moderately severe, improved from 18 at admission). GAD-7: 14 (severe). Cognitive: Orientation improved to x4.
Concentration improving but still impaired. Emerging insight into relapse patterns. Physical: CIWA ≤ 10 for 48 hours. COWS
not applicable — stable on buprenorphine 16mg. Weight 110 lbs (down 2 lbs from admission). Tremor resolving.
Nightmares occurring nightly per patient report. Labs improving: AST 162, ALT 128, platelets 102.
Plan
1. Continue individual therapy 2x/week — next session to focus on safety planning and processing boyfriend's threatening
communications
2. Continue Seeking Safety group
3. Coordinate with case manager re: Denver discharge plan — obtain brother's address, identify IOP programs and
buprenorphine prescribers in Denver area
4. Continue SI monitoring at each clinical contact — consider formal C-SSRS administration
5. Follow up on nutritional concerns — track meal intake, daily weights, ensure dietetics consult completed
6. Update treatment plan at scheduled review (04/10) — add IPV/safety as formal treatment plan problem
7. Coordinate with psychiatry re: prazosin titration and antidepressant consideration
8. Follow up on hepatology consult status — ordered Day 1, not yet documented as completed
9. Explore self-efficacy building through motivational interviewing — reframe prior treatment experiences as learning
rather than failure
10. Begin EMDR readiness assessment once withdrawal fully resolved

sections.data:
Day 12 of treatment. CIWA discontinued — scores ≤ 4 for past 5 days. COWS not applicable, patient stable on
buprenorphine 16mg SL daily. Cravings 3/10. PHQ-9: 14 (moderate, down from 18 at admission). GAD-7: 12 (moderate,
down from 15). Weight: 107 lbs (down 5 lbs from admission weight of 112 lbs, BMI approximately 17.5). Patient has eaten
less than 50% of meals for past several days per nursing documentation. Peer support specialist documented patient
giving away snacks to roommate. Nightmares decreased to 2-3 per week from nightly since prazosin increase to 2mg.
Attending 100% of scheduled groups. Completed initial safety plan with DV advocate. Librium taper completed 04/08. Labs
trending favorably — AST and ALT improving, platelets stable. Hepatology consult ordered Day 1 but no follow-up
documentation in chart. 12 consecutive days of abstinence — patient reports this is longest since age 22.
sections.subjective:
Patient states she feels "weird being sober this long." Reports she spoke with brother by phone and he reiterated his offer
for her to come to Denver: "He said he'd help me find a job and go to meetings with me." Patient tearful but affect notably
brighter than previous sessions. Reports nightmares have decreased since prazosin increase — "I only wake up 2-3 times a
week now instead of every night." States she is "starting to feel things I haven't felt in years — it's scary but maybe not all
bad." Describes emerging emotional awareness as both frightening and encouraging. When asked about appetite, patient
states she "just forgets to eat sometimes" and food doesn't taste right. When asked about suicidal ideation, patient states:
"Honestly, I still have the thoughts sometimes, like it would be easier to not exist. But I don't want to die. I want to figure
out how to live without all this." Reports boyfriend's texts have slowed but she remains anxious. Asked about timeline for
discharge and expressed both hope and fear about next steps.
sections.assessment:
Patient demonstrating meaningful progress across multiple domains. Medical stability achieved — withdrawal resolved,
vital signs normalized, labs trending favorably. Psychological engagement is the strongest of any prior treatment episode
— attending all programming, actively participating in groups, developing therapeutic alliance, and demonstrating
emerging insight into trauma-substance use connection. Passive SI persists but current presentation suggests chronic
ideation connected to trauma history and low self-efficacy rather than acute imminent risk. Patient's statement "I don't
want to die, I want to figure out how to live" represents a significant shift from admission presentation. Denver discharge
plan with brother represents the most viable pathway to sustained recovery — sober environment, family support,
geographic distance from boyfriend and using network. However, geographic change alone is insufficient and must be
paired with continued treatment (IOP), buprenorphine maintenance, trauma therapy, and recovery community
engagement. Weight loss of 5 lbs in 12 days in an already underweight patient with liver disease is concerning and requires
aggressive nutritional follow-up — may be multifactorial (medication side effects, early sobriety anorexia, depression). This
could become a barrier to step-down if not addressed. Outstanding items: hepatology consult follow-up not documented,
formal suicide risk assessment instrument not administered (C-SSRS recommended), cultural assessment not completed,
spiritual assessment incomplete.

documentation in chart. 12 consecutive days of abstinence — patient reports this is longest since age 22.
